title: Satellite data for farm loans: SatSure raises Rs 60 crore from IN-SPACe-anchored fund
summary: SatSure raises Rs 60 crore from IN-SPACe-anchored fund to use satellite data for farm loans
detailed: Bengaluru-based spacetech startup SatSure has raised Rs 60 crore from the Antariksh Venture Capital Fund (AVCF), the government-backed spacetech fund, in the first close of its ongoing Rs 200 crore Series B round.
In June this year, IN-SPACe awarded SatSure a Rs 24.6 crore grant under its Technology Adoption Fund to build Dhaarini.
The government had announced a Rs 1,000 crore venture capital fund for the space sector, and IN-SPACe selected SIDBI Venture Capital as its manager in March 2025.
According to the government, the fund is to be deployed over five years, with an indicative investment range of Rs 10 crore to Rs 60 crore per startup depending on its stage.
sentences: Bengaluru-based spacetech startup SatSure has raised Rs 60 crore from the Antariksh Venture Capital Fund (AVCF), the government-backed spacetech fund, in the first close of its ongoing Rs 200 crore Series B round.
The funding is investing at a post-money valuation of Rs 870 crore, SatSure said.
AVCF is anchored by IN-SPACe, India's private space sector regulator and promoter, and managed by SIDBI Venture Capital Limited, an arm of state-owned small-business lender SIDBI.
The Rs 60 crore cheque accounts for roughly 30% of the planned round.

According to the announcement, the Series B comprises Rs 165 crore in primary equity, Rs 25 crore in venture debt and Rs 10 crore in secondary transactions, and will close on a rolling basis through December 2026.
With the first close, SatSure has raised Rs 427 crore in institutional capital so far, excluding government grants.

SatSure said the capital will go towards four goals: preparing its optical payloads for orbital flight in 2027, executing its multi-satellite constellation mandate under the IN-SPACe-anchored Earth Observation Public-Private Partnership (EO-PPP), scaling Dhaarini, its Large Earth Observation Model, and expanding its international commercial operations from India.
“ The strategic value of the space economy lies not only in reaching orbit, but in what we can understand from it, ” said Prateep Basu, co-founder and CEO of SatSure.
“ We built SatSure to own that full stack end-to-end, and the Series B round lets us build it further, from India, for the world, ” he added.

Founded in 2017 by Prateep Basu, Rashmit Singh Sukhmani and Abhishek Raju, SatSure uses satellite imagery and AI to help banks, insurers, infrastructure companies and government agencies make decisions.
It operates through two entities.
Its subsidiary KaleidEO builds optical satellite payloads, and for the national Earth observation constellation under the EO-PPP, the full satellites.
SatSure itself turns that data into analytics and industry-specific products.

The startup said its SatSource product line is part of the RBI's Unified Lending Interface, where public-sector banks, including the State Bank of India, use it to underwrite farm loans in minutes rather than weeks.
SatSure counts 24 banking and financial services customers.
Its clients include HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank, ITC, Bayer and the Airports Authority of India.
HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank are also shareholders.
In August 2025, SatSure joined a consortium led by Pixxel, along with PierSight and Dhruva Space, that IN-SPACe selected to build India's national Earth observation constellation.
The programme involves 12 multi-sensor satellites over three to five years, with an investment of Rs 1,200 crore.
SatSure will contribute two of those satellites, carrying optical and multispectral wide-swath imagers built by KaleidEO.
In June this year, IN-SPACe awarded SatSure a Rs 24.6 crore grant under its Technology Adoption Fund to build Dhaarini.
SatSure was one of three projects chosen.
According to the startup, Dhaarini is an Earth intelligence system designed to analyse India-specific patterns, including monsoon dynamics, smallholder farming, flood cycles and urban expansion.

When SatSure raised a $15 million Series A in August 2023, led by Baring Private Equity Partners India and Promus Ventures, it said it planned a fleet of four high-resolution optical and multispectral satellites targeted for the fourth quarter of 2025.
Its earlier backers also include Asian Development Bank Ventures, Omidyar Network India (now Prana Ventures), HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank and Nuvama Asset Management.
This is AVCF's first investment in the downstream data analytics and AI layer of India's space economy, after a focus on launch and satellite hardware.
The fund made its first investment in July, putting Rs 60 crore into Hyderabad-based satellite maker Dhruva Space.

“ Leading SatSure's Series B round reflects AVCF's thesis of backing full-stack enterprises that pair indigenous orbital infrastructure with downstream decision intelligence, ” said Arup Kumar, MD and CEO of SIDBI Venture Capital.
The government had announced a Rs 1,000 crore venture capital fund for the space sector, and IN-SPACe selected SIDBI Venture Capital as its manager in March 2025.
The fund now has a corpus of Rs 1,600 crore.
According to the government, the fund is to be deployed over five years, with an indicative investment range of Rs 10 crore to Rs 60 crore per startup depending on its stage.
Both of AVCF's deals so far have been at the top of that range.
The fund is part of India's effort to grow its space economy from an estimated $8.4 billion to $44 billion by 2033.
